    Forecasters¶

    Build a model from the registry and forecast a task with it. See Getting started for a worked example.

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters ¶

    Forecasters: the interface every model meets, the registry and the models.

    • base: ForecastTask, the ForecastModel protocol and the registry.
    • randomwalk: the random walk baseline, and random walk on a nowcast, with chain (the daily chain ladder), pooling, obs and walk.
    • pprandomwalk: random walk on a nowcast with partially pooled estimates (numpyro).
    • renewal: the renewal variants, the adapter from a ForecastTask to the PyRenew model in bdbvhubrenewal.model.
    • zones: health-zone forecasts split from any model's province samples.

    Importing this package registers the built-in models. To add a variant, write a class with name and forecast(task) and call register_model in its module, then import that module here.

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.base ¶

    The forecast task, the model interface and the model registry.

    A model is anything with a name and a forecast(task) method that returns sample trajectories for the task's provinces and weeks. The harness adds the national total, writes hub files, scores and plots. So adding a model variant is one class and one register_model call.

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class ForecastTask:
    """Everything a model sees for one forecast.

    Attributes
    ----------
    vintage : str
        The `as_of` date of the data, ISO format.
    reference_date : datetime.date
        The round's reference date.
    kind : str
        `"real"` or `"simulated"`.
    cutoff : str
        The vintage's data cut-off, its latest onset day, ISO format
        (`bdbvhubrenewal.data.releases.release_cutoff`).
    target : pandas.DataFrame
        The target table rows of this vintage only (columns as in
        `bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy_target`), for the country and
        provinces.
    delays : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Delay line data available at this vintage (see
        `bdbvhubrenewal.data.tidy_delays`), or None if none was published.
    locations : tuple of str
        Provinces to forecast.
    target_end_dates : tuple of str
        Weeks to forecast, ISO Saturdays.
    n_samples : int
        Number of sample trajectories.
    seed : int
        Seed for the model's random numbers.
    mask : tuple of str
        Provinces whose counts the model must not fit to, for the
        leave-one-province-out check. They stay in `locations`, so they
        are still forecast, and in `target`, so a model can keep them in
        its latent process (for spatial coupling) while dropping them from
        its likelihood. Only models with `supports_mask = True` are given
        a non-empty mask.
    report_by : mapping of str to str
        Later vintage dates to their cut-offs, ISO format. A model may also
        return, for each date $T$ here, the counts it predicts will be
        reported by $T$'s cut-off for the weeks ending on or before $T$,
        in rows with `as_of` $= T$. Scoring compares them with vintage
        $T$ as reported.
    delay_history : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Delay rows of every vintage of this kind on or before `vintage`,
        from which `data.releases.release_pairs` gives the rows each file
        kept of the last, which the renewal models learn their report to
        publication lag from. None if there are none.
    target_history : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Target rows of every vintage of this kind on or before `vintage`,
        from which a model can learn how totals are revised. None if there
        are none.
    daily_history : pandas.DataFrame or None
        Daily onsets of every release of this kind on or before `vintage`:
        one row per release, place and onset day with any cases, with
        columns `vintage` (release date), `location`, `onset_date`,
        `observed`, `imputed` and `cutoff` (the release's cut-off). None
        if there are none.
    """

    vintage: str
    reference_date: dt.date
    kind: str
    cutoff: str
    target: pd.DataFrame
    delays: pd.DataFrame | None
    locations: tuple[str, ...]
    target_end_dates: tuple[str, ...]
    n_samples: int = 100
    seed: int = 0
    mask: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    report_by: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    delay_history: pd.DataFrame | None = None
    target_history: pd.DataFrame | None = None
    daily_history: pd.DataFrame | None = None

    def rng(self, *keys: str) -> np.random.Generator:
        """Return a random generator seeded from the task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        *keys : str
            Names that give their own stream, such as a model name, so
            draws for one name do not depend on draws for another.

        Returns
        -------
        numpy.random.Generator
            Seeded from `seed`, the vintage and each key's CRC-32, so tasks
            and keys differ.
        """
        offset = as_date(self.vintage).toordinal()
        names = [zlib.crc32(k.encode()) for k in keys]
        return np.random.default_rng([self.seed, offset, *names])

    def rng(self, *keys: str) -> np.random.Generator:
    """Return a random generator seeded from the task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    *keys : str
        Names that give their own stream, such as a model name, so
        draws for one name do not depend on draws for another.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.random.Generator
        Seeded from `seed`, the vintage and each key's CRC-32, so tasks
        and keys differ.
    """
    offset = as_date(self.vintage).toordinal()
    names = [zlib.crc32(k.encode()) for k in keys]
    return np.random.default_rng([self.seed, offset, *names])

class ModelSpec:
    """A registered model.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Registry key.
    factory : callable
        Builds the model with no arguments.
    description : str
        One line for tables and docs.
    baseline : bool
        Whether this is the reference model for relative scores.
    fitted : bool
        Whether the model is fitted by MCMC for each task, so is slow.
        The docs report and the smoke tests run only models that are not.
    """

    name: str
    factory: Callable[[], ForecastModel]
    description: str
    baseline: bool = False
    fitted: bool = False

    def register_model(
    name: str,
    factory: Callable[[], ForecastModel],
    description: str,
    *,
    baseline: bool = False,
    fitted: bool = False,
    replace: bool = False,
) -> ModelSpec:
    """Add a model to the registry used by the backtest, CLI and docs.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Registry key and model name.
    factory : callable
        Builds the model with no arguments.
    description : str
        One line describing the model.
    baseline : bool
        Mark the model as the baseline for relative skill.
    fitted : bool
        Mark the model as fitted by MCMC for each task.
    replace : bool
        Allow replacing an existing entry.

    Returns
    -------
    ModelSpec
        The registered entry.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `name` is already registered and `replace` is False.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from dataclasses import dataclass
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import register_model
    >>> @dataclass
    ... class Flat:
    ...     name: str = "flat"
    ...     def forecast(self, task):
    ...         ...  # return rows with columns SAMPLE_COLUMNS
    >>> spec = register_model("flat", Flat, "A flat line.")
    """
    if name in _REGISTRY and not replace:
        raise ValueError(f"Model {name!r} is already registered.")
    spec = ModelSpec(name, factory, description, baseline, fitted)
    _REGISTRY[name] = spec
    return spec

    def get_model(name: str) -> ForecastModel:
    """Build a registered model by name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Registry key.

    Returns
    -------
    ForecastModel
        A new instance.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If no model has that name.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import get_model, list_models
    >>> [spec.name for spec in list_models()]
    ['randomwalk', 'randomwalknowcast', 'renewal', 'renewalbvd', 'renewalsp']
    >>> model = get_model("randomwalknowcast")
    >>> samples = model.forecast(task)  # a ForecastTask, see `make_tasks`
    """
    if name not in _REGISTRY:
        raise KeyError(f"No model {name!r}. Known: {sorted(_REGISTRY)}.")
    return _REGISTRY[name].factory()

    def check_samples(samples: pd.DataFrame, task: ForecastTask) -> None:
    """Check a model's output against its task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        Output of `ForecastModel.forecast`. It may include national
        rows, for a model that fits the nation on its own, and `as_of`
        rows for the dates in `task.report_by`.
    task : ForecastTask
        The task it answers.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If columns, locations, weeks or sample numbers do not match, any
        value is negative or missing, or an `as_of` date was not asked
        for.
    """
    columns = tuple(samples.columns)
    if columns not in (SAMPLE_COLUMNS, (*SAMPLE_COLUMNS, "as_of")):
        raise ValueError(f"Columns must be {SAMPLE_COLUMNS}, then `as_of`.")
    weeks = set(task.target_end_dates)
    if "as_of" not in samples:
        _check_block(samples, task, weeks, "")
        return
    as_of = samples["as_of"]
    _check_block(samples.loc[as_of.isna()], task, weeks, "")
    for key, rows in samples.loc[as_of.notna()].groupby("as_of"):
        date = str(key)
        if date not in task.report_by:
            raise ValueError(f"as_of {date} is not in the task's report_by.")
        due = {w for w in weeks if w <= date}
        _check_block(rows, task, due, f" for as_of {date}")

    def add_national(samples: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Add the national total as the sum of provinces by sample.

    A model that fits the nation on its own gives national rows, which
    are kept as they are.

    Parameters
    ----------
    samples : pandas.DataFrame
        Province samples with columns `SAMPLE_COLUMNS`, and optionally
        `as_of`. Each `as_of` is summed on its own.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        The input with `CD` rows appended.
    """
    if (samples["location"] == NATIONAL).any():
        return samples.reset_index(drop=True)
    provinces = samples.loc[samples["location"] != NATIONAL]
    columns = [c for c in samples.columns if c != "location"]
    keys = [c for c in columns if c != "value"]
    national = provinces.groupby(keys, as_index=False, dropna=False)[
        "value"
    ].sum()
    national.insert(0, "location", NATIONAL)
    return pd.concat([provinces, national[list(samples.columns)]]).reset_index(
        drop=True
    )

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.randomwalk ¶

    The random walk baselines.

    Both models run on the hub's daily release snapshots (chain), at province and zone level, from one random walk (walk.random_walk).

    RandomWalk (randomwalk) starts from the reported count of the latest week judged complete, \(\pi \ge 0.95\), where

    \[ \pi(w) = \frac{1}{7} \sum_{t \in w} \frac{\mathbb{1}\{t \le c\}}{G(a(t))} \]

    is the share of the week's final count reported, under the delay estimate of chain. Weeks up to the start are returned as reported. Later weeks are walk draws, floored at the count reported.

    RandomWalkNowcast (randomwalknowcast) nowcasts each hub week, with negative binomial new reports on the remaining count (obs). Each sample starts the walk from its own nowcast of the latest full week at least Settings.start_share reported with at least Settings.start_count cases (_start_weeks). Later weeks with data keep their nowcast draws. If the week holding the cut-off is partial, its days after the cut-off add Poisson draws from that week's walk rate. Weeks after the cut-off are the walk's draws.

    The spread of the walk is the standard deviation of the weekly changes of \(\log(1 + y)\) in reported counts, over the weeks ending at the start of randomwalk, net of their delta-method Poisson noise (walk.walk_variance). A place whose net variance is 0 or below has no own estimate. The delay, the observation model and the walk spread each use their own estimate where a place has at least 10 cases a week, and otherwise the pooled estimate of the nearest parent that does (pooling). A place with no case in the latest walk_weeks weeks is silent. It is exactly 0 until its first introduction, which comes each week with its pooled probability times the share of the week not yet reported, and then walks from a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least 1 (introductions.silent_trajectories). In randomwalknowcast a place with no week to start from is quiet like a silent one: after its latest complete week it draws introductions, floored at the counts reported (_quiet). National is the sum of provinces by sample. Each model raises if the task has no snapshots or no pair of releases within the delay window.

    @dataclass
class RandomWalk:
    """Carry the latest complete week forward with growing noise.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Model name.
    settings : Settings
        Delay window, thresholds and the walk's window.
    fit_diagnostics : list of dict
        One row per place from the last forecast: the start week, the
        errors behind the spread and the source of the delay, spread and
        walk.
    """

    name: str = "randomwalk"
    settings: Settings = field(default_factory=Settings)
    fit_diagnostics: list[dict[str, object]] = field(default_factory=list)
    needs_snapshots: ClassVar[bool] = True

    def origin_at(self, task: ForecastTask, errors: bool) -> Origin:
        """Fit the delays and the walk at the task's vintage.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task. Its `daily_history` holds the release snapshots.
        errors : bool
            Also fit the nowcast errors, which `RandomWalkNowcast` needs.

        Returns
        -------
        Origin
            The fit at the task's vintage.

        Raises
        ------
        MissingSnapshots
            If the task has no release snapshots.
        """
        _clear_caches(task)
        daily = task.daily_history
        if daily is None or daily.empty:
            raise MissingSnapshots(
                f"{self.name} needs daily release snapshots, and the task "
                f"for {task.vintage} has none."
            )
        snap = snapshot_arrays(daily, task.vintage, task.locations)
        return build_origin(snap, self.settings, errors)

    def rows(self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask) -> list[int]:
        """Return the origin's row of each of the task's places.

        Parameters
        ----------
        origin : Origin
            The fit, from `origin_at`.
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        list of int
            Row indices, in the order of `task.locations`.
        """
        pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(origin.snap.locations)}
        return [pos[c] for c in task.locations]

    def _diagnostics(
        self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask, start: np.ndarray
    ) -> None:
        rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
        for loc, i in zip(task.locations, self.rows(origin, task), strict=True):
            n_err = None if origin.obs_n is None else int(origin.obs_n[i, 0])
            obs_src = (
                None
                if origin.obs_source is None
                else _label(origin, int(origin.obs_source[i, 0]))
            )
            rows.append(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "start_week": origin.snap.week_ends[int(start[i])],
                    "n_err": n_err,
                    "delay_source": _label(origin, int(origin.fit.source[i])),
                    "obs_source": obs_src,
                    "sigma_source": _label(origin, int(origin.sigma_source[i])),
                }
            )
        self.fit_diagnostics = rows

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return random walk trajectories for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
            release snapshots.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            If the task has no snapshots, no pair of releases within
            the delay window, or a place with no week that is 95 per cent
            complete (`NoCompleteWeek`).

        Examples
        --------
        >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import get_model
        >>> samples = get_model("randomwalk").forecast(task)
        >>> samples.groupby(["location", "target_end_date"])["value"].median()
        """
        origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=False)
        weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
        n_data, n_all, n = origin.snap.n_weeks, len(weeks), task.n_samples
        n_loc = len(origin.snap.locations)
        good = origin.complete >= origin.settings.completeness
        if not good.any(axis=1).all():
            has = good.any(axis=1)
            none = [
                x
                for x, ok in zip(origin.snap.locations, has, strict=True)
                if not ok
            ]
            raise NoCompleteWeek(
                f"No week reaches {origin.settings.completeness:.0%} "
                f"complete at {origin.snap.releases[origin.o]} for "
                f"{', '.join(none)}, so the walk has no start week."
            )
        start = origin.start
        x0 = origin.reported[np.arange(n_loc), start]
        _, y = _walks(
            _key(task),
            np.repeat(x0[:, None], n, axis=1),
            origin,
            start,
            n_all,
            origin.silent,
        )
        values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
        for loc in range(n_loc):
            for u in range(n_all):
                if u <= start[loc]:
                    values[:, loc, u] = origin.reported[loc, u]
                else:
                    draw = y[loc, :, u - start[loc] - 1]
                    floor = origin.reported[loc, u] if u < n_data else 0.0
                    values[:, loc, u] = np.maximum(draw, floor)
        self._diagnostics(origin, task, start)
        return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

    @dataclass
class RandomWalkNowcast(RandomWalk):
    """The random walk run forward from a daily nowcast of the recent weeks.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Model name.
    delay_summary : pandas.DataFrame or None
        The delay of the last forecast (`chain.delay_summary`), which maps
        its final counts to what later releases show.
    """

    name: str = "randomwalknowcast"
    delay_summary: pd.DataFrame | None = field(
        init=False, default=None, repr=False
    )

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return random walk trajectories from a nowcast for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
            release snapshots.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

        Raises
        ------
        ModelUnavailableError
            If the task has no snapshots, or no pair of releases within
            the delay window.
        """
        origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=True)
        values, weeks = self.trajectories(origin, task, origin.point)
        self.delay_summary = delay_summary(origin, self.name, task.vintage)
        self._diagnostics(
            origin,
            task,
            _start_weeks(origin),
        )
        return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

    def trajectories(
        self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask, point: np.ndarray
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
        """Return trajectories from a nowcast with mean `point`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        origin : Origin
            The fit at the task's vintage, with its observation model.
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.
        point : numpy.ndarray
            Mean weekly nowcast, `[L, W]`. The model's own is
            `origin.point`. A later release's expected count gives the
            prediction scored in the backtest.

        Returns
        -------
        tuple
            Samples `[S, L, H]` for every hub week from the first data
            week to the last target, and those weeks.
        """
        snap = origin.snap
        assert origin.size is not None
        weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
        n_data, n_all, n = snap.n_weeks, len(weeks), task.n_samples
        n_loc = len(snap.locations)
        k_n = origin.size.shape[1]
        back = snap.cut_week(origin.o) - np.arange(n_data)
        # Weeks older than the fitted ones have nothing to come.
        k = np.clip(back, 0, k_n - 1)
        key_x, key_walk, key_part = jax.random.split(_key(task), 3)
        shape = (n, *point.shape)
        reported = jnp.broadcast_to(
            jnp.asarray(origin.reported, jnp.float32), shape
        )
        nowcast = np.asarray(
            sample_count(
                key_x,
                reported,
                jnp.maximum(jnp.asarray(point, jnp.float32) - reported, 0.0),
                jnp.broadcast_to(
                    jnp.asarray(origin.size[:, k], jnp.float32), shape
                ),
            ),
            np.float64,
        )
        # Each sample walks on from its own nowcast of the start week.
        cw = snap.cut_week(origin.o)
        w0 = _start_weeks(origin)
        quiet = _quiet(origin)
        rows = np.arange(n_loc)
        lam, y = _walks(
            key_walk, nowcast[:, rows, w0].T, origin, w0, n_all, quiet
        )
        # Days of the cut-off week after the cut-off are drawn from the
        # walk's rate that week.
        cut = int(snap.cut[origin.o])
        miss = int(np.flatnonzero(snap.week == cw).max()) - cut
        at_cw = np.clip(cw - w0 - 1, 0, n_all - 1)
        part = np.asarray(
            jax.random.poisson(
                key_part,
                jnp.asarray(lam[rows, :, at_cw] * miss / 7, jnp.float32),
            ),
            dtype=np.float64,
        )  # [L, S]
        values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
        for loc in range(n_loc):
            s = int(w0[loc])
            if quiet[loc]:
                # A quiet place is its reported counts, then its
                # introductions, floored at the counts reported.
                values[:, loc, : s + 1] = origin.reported[loc, : s + 1]
                values[:, loc, s + 1 :] = y[loc, :, : n_all - s - 1]
                values[:, loc, :n_data] = np.maximum(
                    values[:, loc, :n_data], origin.reported[loc]
                )
                continue
            values[:, loc, : cw + 1] = nowcast[:, loc, : cw + 1]
            if miss > 0 and cw > s:
                values[:, loc, cw] += part[loc]
            values[:, loc, cw + 1 :] = y[loc, :, cw - s : n_all - s - 1]
        return values, weeks

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return random walk trajectories from a nowcast for a task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The data and weeks to forecast. Its `daily_history` holds the
        release snapshots.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `location`, `target_end_date`, `sample`, `value`.

    Raises
    ------
    ModelUnavailableError
        If the task has no snapshots, or no pair of releases within
        the delay window.
    """
    origin = self.origin_at(task, errors=True)
    values, weeks = self.trajectories(origin, task, origin.point)
    self.delay_summary = delay_summary(origin, self.name, task.vintage)
    self._diagnostics(
        origin,
        task,
        _start_weeks(origin),
    )
    return frame(task, weeks, values, self.rows(origin, task))

    def trajectories(
    self, origin: Origin, task: ForecastTask, point: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, list[str]]:
    """Return trajectories from a nowcast with mean `point`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    origin : Origin
        The fit at the task's vintage, with its observation model.
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.
    point : numpy.ndarray
        Mean weekly nowcast, `[L, W]`. The model's own is
        `origin.point`. A later release's expected count gives the
        prediction scored in the backtest.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple
        Samples `[S, L, H]` for every hub week from the first data
        week to the last target, and those weeks.
    """
    snap = origin.snap
    assert origin.size is not None
    weeks = _timeline(origin, task)
    n_data, n_all, n = snap.n_weeks, len(weeks), task.n_samples
    n_loc = len(snap.locations)
    k_n = origin.size.shape[1]
    back = snap.cut_week(origin.o) - np.arange(n_data)
    # Weeks older than the fitted ones have nothing to come.
    k = np.clip(back, 0, k_n - 1)
    key_x, key_walk, key_part = jax.random.split(_key(task), 3)
    shape = (n, *point.shape)
    reported = jnp.broadcast_to(
        jnp.asarray(origin.reported, jnp.float32), shape
    )
    nowcast = np.asarray(
        sample_count(
            key_x,
            reported,
            jnp.maximum(jnp.asarray(point, jnp.float32) - reported, 0.0),
            jnp.broadcast_to(
                jnp.asarray(origin.size[:, k], jnp.float32), shape
            ),
        ),
        np.float64,
    )
    # Each sample walks on from its own nowcast of the start week.
    cw = snap.cut_week(origin.o)
    w0 = _start_weeks(origin)
    quiet = _quiet(origin)
    rows = np.arange(n_loc)
    lam, y = _walks(
        key_walk, nowcast[:, rows, w0].T, origin, w0, n_all, quiet
    )
    # Days of the cut-off week after the cut-off are drawn from the
    # walk's rate that week.
    cut = int(snap.cut[origin.o])
    miss = int(np.flatnonzero(snap.week == cw).max()) - cut
    at_cw = np.clip(cw - w0 - 1, 0, n_all - 1)
    part = np.asarray(
        jax.random.poisson(
            key_part,
            jnp.asarray(lam[rows, :, at_cw] * miss / 7, jnp.float32),
        ),
        dtype=np.float64,
    )  # [L, S]
    values = np.zeros((n, n_loc, n_all))
    for loc in range(n_loc):
        s = int(w0[loc])
        if quiet[loc]:
            # A quiet place is its reported counts, then its
            # introductions, floored at the counts reported.
            values[:, loc, : s + 1] = origin.reported[loc, : s + 1]
            values[:, loc, s + 1 :] = y[loc, :, : n_all - s - 1]
            values[:, loc, :n_data] = np.maximum(
                values[:, loc, :n_data], origin.reported[loc]
            )
            continue
        values[:, loc, : cw + 1] = nowcast[:, loc, : cw + 1]
        if miss > 0 and cw > s:
            values[:, loc, cw] += part[loc]
        values[:, loc, cw + 1 :] = y[loc, :, cw - s : n_all - s - 1]
    return values, weeks

    def frame(
    task: ForecastTask, weeks: list[str], values: np.ndarray, rows: list[int]
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return sample rows from `values` of shape `[S, L, H]`."""
    col = {w: i for i, w in enumerate(weeks)}
    targets = list(task.target_end_dates)
    n = values.shape[0]
    frames = []
    for loc, row in zip(task.locations, rows, strict=True):
        picked = np.column_stack(
            [
                values[:, row, col[w]] if w in col else np.zeros(n)
                for w in targets
            ]
        )
        frames.append(
            pd.DataFrame(
                {
                    "location": loc,
                    "target_end_date": np.tile(targets, n),
                    "sample": np.repeat(np.arange(1, n + 1), len(targets)),
                    "value": np.maximum(np.round(picked), 0.0).reshape(-1),
                }
            )
        )
    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)[list(SAMPLE_COLUMNS)]

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.chain ¶

    Daily chain ladder on release snapshots, with its uncertainty.

    Counts \(N_r(t)\) are the daily onsets of release \(r\), on the onset clock. Release \(r\) has cut-off \(c_r\), and day \(t\) is \(a = c_r - t\) days old. A pair of consecutive releases \((r, r + 1)\) has step \(s = c_{r+1} - c_r\) days and is in window when \(s \le D\).

    Delay. Releases are batched reports of one daily delay. A day of age \(a\) at release \(r\) grows by \(\exp \sum_{j=a}^{a+s-1} g(j)\) to release \(r + 1\), with \(g(j) \ge 0\) the daily log development factor and \(g(j) = 0\) for \(j \ge D\). For each gap \(s\) and age \(a\), the ratio of sums \(\sum N_{r+1}(t) / \sum N_r(t)\), over the in-window pairs of that gap and the days of age \(a\) that both releases observe, gives one equation for \(\sum_{j=a}^{a+s-1} g(j)\) on the log scale, weighted by the denominator. \(g\) is the non-negative least squares fit of all of them (log_factors). Cells a release does not observe are skipped, not filled. A place with at least 10 cases a week uses its own \(g\), and otherwise the pooled \(g\) of its nearest parent with them, fitted to the summed pair sums of that parent's places with 10 cases a week (pooling), as for the walk spread and the nowcast size. Only onset days within Settings.history_delay (63 for \(D = 42\)) of the latest cut-off are summed, and downward revisions are first moved onto earlier releases of the day, as baselinenowcast does.

    Nowcast. At the latest release \(o\), day \(t\) of age \(a\) grows to final by \(G(a) = \exp \sum_{j=a}^{D-1} g(j)\). Each hub week is a row of a weekly reporting triangle, with a column every 7 days, and the mean over its observed days of \(1 / G\) at each column is the share of the week reported by it. baselinenowcast's apply_delay fills the row from the week's reported count (week_nowcast), with its \(+1\), so a week with nothing reported yet still expects some cases.

    Uncertainty. A release \(r < o\) with an in-window pair at \(r\), and a cut-off at most Settings.retro_delay (63) days before \(c_o\), nowcasts the count expected at \(o\) for days up to \(c_r\), with the same weekly fill from \(c_r\) to \(c_o\) and the \(g\) of \(r\). Its new reports by weeks back fit the observation model (obs), on counts whose downward revisions are moved onto earlier releases, as for the delay.

    Introductions. A place with no case in the latest walk_weeks weeks is silent. Its weekly probability of an introduction is the rate of a first case, or of a re-introduction if it was seen before, over the walk_weeks weeks to its start week, or all weeks to it if those have none, pooled over its siblings (introductions.introduction_rates).

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    """Settings shared by the random walk models.

    Attributes
    ----------
    max_delay : int
        $D$, the days a count may still grow, baselinenowcast's
        `max_delay`.
    min_level : float
        Cases a week for a place to use its own delay, walk spread and
        nowcast size (`pooling`).
    level_weeks : tuple of int
        First and last weeks back averaged for a place's level.
    completeness : float
        Share of a week's final count that must be reported for it to
        start the random walk.
    walk_weeks : int
        Weeks, ending at the start week, whose changes set the spread.
    start_share : float
        Share of a week reported for `randomwalknowcast` to start
        its walk from the week's nowcast.
    start_count : float
        Cases reported in a week for `randomwalknowcast` to start its walk
        from the week's nowcast.
    """

    max_delay: int = 42
    min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL
    level_weeks: tuple[int, int] = (3, 6)
    completeness: float = 0.95
    walk_weeks: int = 9
    start_share: float = 0.05
    start_count: float = 5.0

    @property
    def history_delay(self) -> int:
        """Onset days used for the delay, baselinenowcast's default.

        R uses `floor(0.5 * round(3 * D))` reference times for the delay,
        at least `D + 1`, and the rest for the uncertainty.
        """
        n_used = round(3 * self.max_delay)
        return max(n_used // 2, self.max_delay + 1)

    @property
    def retro_delay(self) -> int:
        """Days back from the origin's cut-off for retrospective nowcasts.

        R gives the `round(3 * D)` reference times left after
        `history_delay` to its retrospective nowcasts, so a release whose
        cut-off is more than this many days before the origin's gives
        none.
        """
        return round(3 * self.max_delay) - self.history_delay

    @property
    def start_nowcast(self) -> int:
        """Latest week whose seven days are all on or before the cut-off."""
        sat = np.array(
            [
                np.flatnonzero(self.snap.week == w).max()
                for w in range(self.snap.n_weeks)
            ]
        )
        full = np.flatnonzero(sat <= self.snap.cut[self.o])
        return int(full.max()) if full.size else 0

    def weeks_back(snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, max_delay: int) -> int:
    r"""Return the number of weeks back from the cut-off week with young days.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        Release index.
    max_delay : int
        $D$.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        $K$: weeks back $k = 0, \dots, K - 1$ hold a day younger than
        $D$.
    """
    youngest = max(int(snap.cut[r]) - max_delay + 1, 0)
    return snap.cut_week(r) - int(snap.week[youngest]) + 1

    def levels(snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, settings: Settings) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return mean weekly counts over the level weeks at release `r`."""
    weekly = weekly_sums(snap, r)
    wa = snap.cut_week(r)
    lo, hi = settings.level_weeks
    cols = [wa - k for k in range(lo, hi + 1)]
    vals = [weekly[:, c] if c >= 0 else np.zeros(weekly.shape[0]) for c in cols]
    return np.mean(vals, axis=0)

    def delay_sums(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, settings: Settings
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    """Return the pair sums the delay is fitted to at release `r`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        Release index. Pairs of later releases are not used.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of numpy.ndarray or None
        The in-window pairs `[P, 2]`, `num` and `den` from `pair_sums`
        `[L, P, D]`, and each pair's gap `[P]`, or None with no
        in-window pair.
    """
    pairs = _pairs_at(snap, r, settings.max_delay)
    if pairs.size == 0:
        return None
    counts = _delay_counts(snap, r)
    day = np.arange(snap.week.size)
    window = day > int(snap.cut[r]) - settings.history_delay
    observed = snap.observed & window[None, :]
    gaps = snap.cut[pairs[:, 1]] - snap.cut[pairs[:, 0]]
    num, den = pair_sums(
        jnp.asarray(counts),
        jnp.asarray(observed),
        jnp.asarray(snap.cut),
        jnp.asarray(pairs[:, 0]),
        settings.max_delay,
    )
    return pairs, np.asarray(num), np.asarray(den), gaps

    den: np.ndarray, parent: np.ndarray, settings: Settings

    Parameters
    ----------
    den : numpy.ndarray

        pairs, is at least `Settings.min_level` cases. The country is

    def fit_delay(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, settings: Settings
) -> DelayFit | None:
    """Estimate the delay factors from the pairs up to release `r`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        Release index. Pairs of later releases are not used.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.

    Returns
    -------
    DelayFit or None
        The factors, or None with no in-window pair.
    """
    sums = delay_sums(snap, r, settings)
    if sums is None:
        return None
    pairs, num, den, gaps = sums
    level = levels(snap, r, settings)
    pool = pool_matrix(level, snap.parent, settings.min_level)
    own_g = log_factors(num, den, gaps)
    pooled_g = log_factors(
        np.einsum("nm,mpa->npa", pool, num),
        np.einsum("nm,mpa->npa", pool, den),
        gaps,
    )
    source = source_index(level, snap.parent, min_level=settings.min_level)
    g = np.concatenate([own_g, pooled_g])[source]
    own = np.broadcast_to((source == np.arange(level.size))[:, None], g.shape)
    return DelayFit(pairs, g, level, source, np.array(own))

    def delay_summary(origin: Origin, model: str, vintage: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return the share of a day's final count reported by each age.

    The share at age $a$ is $1 / G(a)$, from the delay fitted at the
    origin, for every place, in the form of the renewal models' delay
    summaries (`bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.renewal.fit_delays`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    origin : Origin
        The fit.
    model : str
        Model name.
    vintage : str
        The origin.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `model`, `vintage`, `location`, `kind` (`"cumulative"`),
        `x` (age in days), `quantity` (`"reported_share"`) and `q50`.
    """
    ages = np.arange(origin.settings.max_delay + 1)
    share = 1.0 / growth(origin.fit.g, ages, origin.settings.max_delay)
    places = origin.snap.locations
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "model": model,
            "vintage": vintage,
            "location": np.repeat(places, ages.size),
            "kind": "cumulative",
            "x": np.tile(ages, len(places)),
            "quantity": "reported_share",
            "q50": share.ravel(),
        }
    )

    def week_nowcast(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, r: int, g: np.ndarray, age: np.ndarray, gap: int
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return baselinenowcast's count of each hub week `gap` days after `r`.

    Each hub week is a reference time of a weekly reporting triangle,
    with a column every 7 days from the cut-off of release `r` and a last
    one at `gap`.
    The share of the week reported by a column is the mean, over the
    week's days observed at `r`, of their growth from that column to
    `gap` inverted.
    R's `apply_delay` fills each row from these shares (`fill_row`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    r : int
        The release.
    g : numpy.ndarray
        Daily log factors at `r`, `[L, D]`.
    age : numpy.ndarray
        Age of each day at `r`, `[T]`.
    gap : int
        Days from the cut-off of `r` to the count nowcast. `max_delay`
        or more gives the final count.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L, W]`, 0 for weeks with no day observed at `r`.
    """
    seen = np.broadcast_to(snap.observed[r], snap.counts[:, r, :].shape)
    x = week_sum(snap, np.where(seen, snap.counts[:, r, :], 0.0))
    n = week_sum(snap, seen.astype(float))
    steps = np.r_[np.arange(0, gap, 7), gap]
    share = np.stack(
        [
            week_sum(
                snap, np.where(seen, 1.0 / growth(g, age + s, age + gap), 0)
            )
            for s in steps
        ],
        axis=-1,
    )
    cdf = np.where(n[..., None] > 0, share / np.maximum(n, 1)[..., None], 1.0)
    return np.where(n > 0, fill_row(x, cdf), 0.0)

    def retro_errors(
    snap: SnapshotArrays, o: int, settings: Settings, delay: DelayFn = fit_delay
) -> Errors:
    """Collect the errors of nowcasts made at earlier releases.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays.
    o : int
        The origin release.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.
    delay : callable
        Fits the delay at each earlier release.

    Returns
    -------
    Errors
        Sums over the releases that give errors.
    """
    n_loc = len(snap.locations)
    k_n = weeks_back(snap, o, settings.max_delay)
    # As baselinenowcast preprocesses its triangle, a fall is taken from
    # the earlier releases' counts, so a week's count never falls.
    pre = replace(snap, counts=_delay_counts(snap, o))
    cells: list[tuple[np.ndarray, ...]] = []
    releases: list[str] = []
    for r in range(1, o):
        if snap.cut[o] - snap.cut[r] > settings.retro_delay:
            continue
        fit = delay(snap, r, settings)
        if fit is None:
            continue
        age = snap.cut[r] - np.arange(snap.week.size)
        ahead = week_nowcast(pre, r, fit.g, age, snap.cut[o] - snap.cut[r])
        wa, k_r = snap.cut_week(r), weeks_back(snap, r, settings.max_delay)
        cols = wa - np.arange(k_n)
        take = (cols >= 0) & (np.arange(k_n) < k_r)
        safe = np.clip(cols, 0, None)
        obs = weekly_sums(pre, r)[:, safe]
        pred = ahead[:, safe]
        # The week's change to the origin, on days up to the cut-off of r.
        added = weekly_sums(pre, o, upto=int(snap.cut[r]))[:, safe] - obs
        valid = take[None, :] & ((obs > 0) | (pred > 0))
        cells.append((added, pred - obs, obs, valid))
        releases.append(snap.releases[r])
    c = np.array(cells, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 4, n_loc, k_n)
    return Errors(c[:, 0], c[:, 1], c[:, 2], c[:, 3] > 0, releases)

    def build_origin(
    snap: SnapshotArrays,
    settings: Settings,
    errors: bool,
    delay: DelayFn = fit_delay,
) -> Origin:
    """Fit the delay and the walk spread at the latest release.

    Parameters
    ----------
    snap : SnapshotArrays
        The arrays. The origin is the latest release.
    settings : Settings
        Settings.
    errors : bool
        Whether to fit the observation model.
    delay : callable
        Fits the delay at a release.

    Returns
    -------
    Origin
        The fit.

    Raises
    ------
    NoDelayPair
        If no pair of releases has a step within the delay window.
    """
    o = len(snap.releases) - 1
    fit = delay(snap, o, settings)
    if fit is None:
        raise NoDelayPair(
            f"No pair of releases up to {snap.releases[o]} has a step of at "
            f"most {settings.max_delay} days."
        )
    g = final_growth(snap, o, fit, settings)
    reported = weekly_sums(snap, o)
    age = snap.cut[o] - np.arange(snap.week.size)
    point = week_nowcast(snap, o, fit.g, age, settings.max_delay)
    inv = np.where(snap.observed[o][None, :], 1.0 / g, 0.0)
    complete = week_sum(snap, inv) / 7.0
    good = complete >= settings.completeness
    start = np.where(
        good.any(axis=1), snap.n_weeks - 1 - np.argmax(good[:, ::-1], axis=1), 0
    )
    own, pooled = _walk_spreads(reported, start, snap, fit.level, settings)
    # A variance of 0 or below is no estimate, so the place takes its
    # nearest parent's, as one without the level does.
    sigma_source = source_index(
        fit.level,
        snap.parent,
        (own > 0).astype(int)[:, None],
        (pooled > 0).astype(int)[:, None],
        settings.min_level,
        1,
    )[:, 0]
    var = np.concatenate([own, pooled])[sigma_source]
    if not (var > 0).all():
        none = [
            c for c, v in zip(snap.locations, var, strict=True) if not v > 0
        ]
        raise NoWalkSpread(
            f"No walk spread above 0 at {snap.releases[o]} for "
            f"{', '.join(none)}, of its own or from any parent."
        )
    sigma = np.sqrt(var)
    k = settings.walk_weeks
    silent = silent_places(reported, snap.cut_week(o), k)
    intro = introduction_rates(reported, start, snap.parent, k)
    origin = Origin(
        snap, o, settings, fit, g, reported, point, complete, start, sigma,
        sigma_source, silent, intro,
    )  # fmt: skip
    if errors:
        _add_spread(origin)
    return origin

    def walk_changes(
    reported: np.ndarray, start: np.ndarray, settings: Settings
) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    """Return each place's weekly changes of log(1 + y) up to its start week.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reported : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly reported counts, `[L, W]`.
    start : numpy.ndarray
        Start week of each place, `[L]`.
    settings : Settings
        Settings, for `walk_weeks`.

    Returns
    -------
    list of numpy.ndarray
        The changes of each place over the `walk_weeks` weeks ending at
        its start week.
    """
    diffs = []
    for n in range(reported.shape[0]):
        lo = max(int(start[n]) - settings.walk_weeks + 1, 0)
        diffs.append(np.diff(np.log1p(reported[n, lo : int(start[n]) + 1])))
    return diffs

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.introductions ¶

    Introductions into places with no recent cases.

    A place with no case reported in the latest k weeks is silent (silent_places). It is exactly 0 until its first introduction. An introduction comes each week with probability \(q\) times the share of the week not yet reported (introduction_rates). \(q\) is the rate of a first case for a place with none yet, and of a re-introduction for a place seen before, over the k weeks to the place's start week, or all weeks to it where the pool has no introduction in them, pooled over the place and its siblings. It brings a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least 1, and the place then walks on \(\log(1 + y)\) with its walk spread (silent_trajectories).

    def silent_places(reported: np.ndarray, cut_week: int, k: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the places with no case in the `k` weeks to `cut_week`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reported : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly reported counts, `[L, W]`.
    cut_week : int
        Index of the week holding the cut-off.
    k : int
        Weeks without a case.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L]`, true where silent.
    """
    recent = reported[:, cut_week - k + 1 : cut_week + 1]
    return np.asarray(recent.sum(axis=1) == 0)

    def introduction_rates(
    reported: np.ndarray, start: np.ndarray, parent: np.ndarray, k: int
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return each place's weekly probability of an introduction.

    A place with no case yet takes the rate of a first case: the weeks
    with a case over the weeks with none before them.
    A place seen before takes the rate of a re-introduction: the weeks
    with a case over the weeks with an earlier case but none in the `k`
    weeks before them.
    Each rate pools the place and its siblings, the children of its
    parent, so zones pool within their province.
    The country has no siblings, so it is a group of its own.
    Each rate counts the `k` weeks to each place's start week, the weeks
    that set the spread of the walk.
    Where the pool has no introduction of that kind in them, all weeks to
    the start week count instead.
    Only complete weeks before the origin are used.

    Parameters
    ----------
    reported : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly reported counts, `[L, W]`.
    start : numpy.ndarray
        Start week of each place, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each place's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    k : int
        Weeks counted, and silent weeks before a re-introduction.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L]`, 0 where the pool has no week at risk.
    """
    pos = reported > 0
    before = np.cumsum(np.pad(pos, ((0, 0), (1, 0))), axis=1)[:, :-1]
    week = np.arange(pos.shape[1])[None, :]
    upto = week <= start[:, None]
    window = upto & (week > start[:, None] - k)
    quiet = np.zeros_like(pos)
    quiet[:, k:] = before[:, k:] == before[:, :-k]
    fresh, seen = upto & (before == 0), upto & quiet & (before > 0)
    first = _pooled(fresh & window, fresh, pos, parent)
    again = _pooled(seen & window, seen, pos, parent)
    return np.where(pos.any(axis=1), again, first)

    def silent_trajectories(
    key: jax.Array,
    silent: np.ndarray,
    q: np.ndarray,
    unreported: np.ndarray,
    start: np.ndarray,
    sigma: np.ndarray,
    h: int,
    n: int,
) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Draw the counts of silent places after their start week.

    A silent place is exactly 0 until its first introduction.
    Week `start + 1 + i` brings one with probability $q$ times the share
    of the week not yet reported, so an introduction is likelier in
    recent weeks, whose cases may still be reported, and has probability
    $q$ in weeks without data.
    The introduction brings a count drawn from Poisson(1) given at least
    1, and the place then walks on $\log(1 + y)$ with spread `sigma`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    silent : numpy.ndarray
        True where a place is silent, `[L]`.
    q : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly probability of a first case (`introduction_rates`), `[L]`.
    unreported : numpy.ndarray
        Share of each week not yet reported, `[L, W]`.
        Weeks after `W` are wholly unreported.
    start : numpy.ndarray
        Week after which the counts are drawn, `[L]`.
    sigma : numpy.ndarray
        Standard deviation of a weekly walk step, `[L]`.
    h : int
        Weeks to draw.
    n : int
        Samples to draw.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Counts for weeks `start + 1` to `start + h`, `[L, n, h]`, and 0
        for places that are not silent.
    """
    out = np.zeros((silent.size, n, h))
    idx = np.flatnonzero(silent)
    if idx.size == 0:
        return out
    u = start[idx, None] + 1 + np.arange(h)[None, :]
    share = np.take_along_axis(
        np.pad(unreported[idx], ((0, 0), (0, h + 1)), constant_values=1.0),
        u,
        axis=1,
    )
    k_walk, k_intro, k_count = jax.random.split(key, 3)
    v = np.asarray(jax.random.uniform(k_count, (idx.size, n)), np.float64)
    x0 = stats.poisson.ppf(np.exp(-1.0) + v * -np.expm1(-1.0), 1.0)
    keys = jax.random.split(k_walk, idx.size)
    _, drawn = random_walks(
        keys,
        jnp.asarray(x0, jnp.float32),
        jnp.asarray(sigma[idx], jnp.float32),
        h,
    )
    y = np.asarray(drawn, dtype=np.float64)
    hit = np.asarray(jax.random.uniform(k_intro, (idx.size, n, h))) < (
        q[idx, None, None] * share[:, None, :]
    )
    first = np.where(hit.any(axis=2), np.argmax(hit, axis=2), h)
    lag = np.arange(h)[None, None, :] - first[:, :, None]
    # The introduced count is the first week's, and the walk from it
    # gives the weeks after.
    walked = np.take_along_axis(y, np.clip(lag - 1, 0, h - 1), axis=2)
    paths = np.where(lag >= 1, walked, 0.0)
    out[idx] = np.where(lag == 0, x0[:, :, None], paths)
    return out

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.pooling ¶

    The one own-or-pooled rule.

    Places form a hierarchy, zone then province then country. Each node has an own estimate, from its own counts, errors or weekly changes, and a pooled estimate, from its children with a level of at least min_level cases a week. A parent's counts are the sum of its children's, so the parent is not in its own pool unless no child qualifies. A node counts as qualifying when its level is at least min_level, and for the walk spread also when its estimate exists (a net variance above 0). A qualifying node uses its own estimate. Otherwise it uses the pooled estimate of its nearest ancestor that qualifies, else the country's pooled estimate. The delay, the spread of the walk and the observation model all use this rule with one threshold.

    def pool_matrix(
    level: np.ndarray, parent: np.ndarray, min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the matrix that sums a node's qualifying children.

    Parameters
    ----------
    level : numpy.ndarray
        Cases a week of each node, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each node's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    min_level : float
        Level at which a child enters its parent's pool.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        `[L, L]`, with entry `[n, m]` 1 if $m$ is a child of $n$ with a
        level of at least `min_level`, or if $m = n$ and no child of $n$
        qualifies.
    """
    n = len(level)
    out = np.zeros((n, n))
    for m in range(n):
        if parent[m] >= 0 and level[m] >= min_level:
            out[parent[m], m] = 1.0
    alone = out.sum(axis=1) == 0
    out[alone, alone] = 1.0
    return out

    def source_index(
    level: np.ndarray,
    parent: np.ndarray,
    n_own: np.ndarray | None = None,
    n_pooled: np.ndarray | None = None,
    min_level: float = MIN_LEVEL,
    min_err: int = 1,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return the node whose estimate each node uses.

    Parameters
    ----------
    level : numpy.ndarray
        Cases a week of each node, `[L]`.
    parent : numpy.ndarray
        Index of each node's parent, or -1, `[L]`.
    n_own, n_pooled : numpy.ndarray, optional
        Errors behind each node's own and pooled estimates, `[L, K]`.
        Without them, only the level counts and the result is `[L]`.
    min_level : float
        Level at which a node qualifies.
    min_err : int
        Errors a node's estimate needs, where they are given.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        Integer index `i`, `[L]` or `[L, K]`. It is an index into the
        own estimates for `i < L` and into the pooled estimates for
        `i >= L`, as `i - L`. Each estimate is gathered with it.
    """
    level = np.asarray(level, dtype=float)
    parent = np.asarray(parent, dtype=int)
    n = level.size
    big = (level >= min_level)[:, None]
    if n_own is None or n_pooled is None:
        ok_own, ok_pool = big, big
    else:
        ok_own = big & (np.asarray(n_own) >= min_err)
        ok_pool = big & (np.asarray(n_pooled) >= min_err)
    k_n = ok_own.shape[1]
    out = np.empty((n, k_n), dtype=int)
    for node in range(n):
        root = node
        while parent[root] >= 0:
            root = parent[root]
        for k in range(k_n):
            if ok_own[node, k]:
                out[node, k] = node
                continue
            a = parent[node]
            while a >= 0 and not ok_pool[a, k]:
                a = parent[a]
            out[node, k] = n + (a if a >= 0 else root)
    return out[:, 0] if n_own is None or n_pooled is None else out

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.obs ¶

    Observation model: new reports on the count still to come.

    For a week with count \(Y\) reported so far and a nowcast mean \(\mu\), the count still to come is \(\mathrm{rem} = \mu - Y \ge 0\). The count at a later release is

    \[ X = Y + A, \qquad A \sim \mathrm{NB}(\mathrm{rem}, \phi_k), \]

    baselinenowcast's negative binomial on the remaining count, fitted and drawn with the port's fit_nb and sample_nb through fit_by_horizon, one size \(\phi_k\) for each week back \(k\). As in baselinenowcast, downward revisions are moved onto earlier releases before the fit (chain._delay_counts), so new reports only add.

    MAX_SIZE module-attribute ¶

    MAX_SIZE = 1000.0

    Upper bound of fit_nb's size, the Poisson end of its range.

    PRIOR_SIZE module-attribute ¶

    PRIOR_SIZE = 1.0 / 0.6745 ** 2

    Size with no errors to fit one, about 2.2.

    It is the median of epinowcast's prior \(1 / \sqrt{\phi} \sim \mathcal{N}^+(0, 1)\).

    def fit_sizes(added: np.ndarray, remaining: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Fit the size $\phi_k$ of each week back by maximum likelihood.

    Parameters
    ----------
    added : numpy.ndarray
        New reports after each retrospective nowcast, `[N, K]`.
    remaining : numpy.ndarray
        Nowcast of the count still to come, `[N, K]`. A cell with 0 and
        no new reports adds nothing to the likelihood, so it pads.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $\phi_k$, `[K]`.
    """
    fitted = np.asarray(fit_by_horizon(added, remaining))
    return np.where((remaining > 0).any(axis=0), fitted, PRIOR_SIZE)

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.walk ¶

    The random walk, one function for both models.

    From start value \(x_i\) per sample, for \(h \ge 1\),

    \[ \log(1 + \lambda_i(h)) = \max\Big(0, \log(1 + x_i) + \sum_{j=1}^{h} \epsilon_{i,j}\Big), \quad \epsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2), \]
    \[ y_i(h) \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i(h)). \]

    Steps are cumulative within a sample, so each sample is one trajectory.

    The spread \(\sigma\) comes from the weekly changes \(\Delta_t\) of \(\log(1 + y_t)\) in reported counts, net of their Poisson noise,

    \[ \sigma^2 = \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\Delta_t) - \overline{v(y_{t-1}) + v(y_t)}, \quad v(y) = \frac{y}{(1 + y)^2}, \]

    where \(v\) is the delta-method variance of \(\log(1 + Y)\) for \(Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)\), \(\lambda / (1 + \lambda)^2\), with the observed count for \(\lambda\) (walk_variance). The walk draws its Poisson counts on top, so the noise is not counted twice.

    def walk_noise(y: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    r"""Return the Poisson noise variance of each change of log(1 + y).

    Parameters
    ----------
    y : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly counts, `[W]`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpy.ndarray
        $v(y_{t-1}) + v(y_t)$ for each change, `[W - 1]`, with
        $v(y) = y / (1 + y)^2$ the delta-method variance of
        $\log(1 + Y)$ for $Y \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(y)$.
    """
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float)
    v = y / (1.0 + y) ** 2
    return v[1:] + v[:-1]

    def walk_variance(changes: np.ndarray, noise: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Return the variance of the walk's steps net of Poisson noise.

    Parameters
    ----------
    changes : numpy.ndarray
        Weekly changes of log(1 + y), `[N]`.
    noise : numpy.ndarray
        Their Poisson noise variances (`walk_noise`), `[N]`.

    Returns
    -------
    float
        The sample variance of `changes` less the mean of `noise`. It
        may be 0 or below, which says the changes hold no more than
        Poisson noise. NaN with fewer than 2 changes.
    """
    if changes.size < 2:
        return float("nan")
    return float(np.var(changes, ddof=1)) - float(np.mean(noise))

    def random_walk(
    key: Array, x0: Array, sigma: Array | float, h: int
) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
    r"""Draw the walk forward on the log scale with Poisson counts.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : jax.Array
        Random key.
    x0 : jax.Array
        Start value of each sample, shape `[S]`.
    sigma : float or jax.Array
        Standard deviation of a weekly step.
    h : int
        Weeks to draw.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of jax.Array
        The rate $\lambda$ and the Poisson count, each `[S, h]`.
    """
    k_step, k_count = jax.random.split(key)
    steps = sigma * jax.random.normal(k_step, (x0.shape[0], h), x0.dtype)
    level = jnp.log1p(x0)[:, None] + jnp.cumsum(steps, axis=1)
    lam = jnp.expm1(jnp.maximum(level, 0.0))
    return lam, jax.random.poisson(k_count, lam).astype(x0.dtype)

    @partial(jax.jit, static_argnums=3)
def random_walks(
    keys: Array, x0: Array, sigma: Array, h: int
) -> tuple[Array, Array]:
    """Draw `random_walk` for each place, compiled as one program.

    Parameters
    ----------
    keys : jax.Array
        One random key per place, `[L]`.
    x0 : jax.Array
        Start values, `[L, S]`.
    sigma : jax.Array
        Step standard deviation of each place, `[L]`.
    h : int
        Weeks to draw.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of jax.Array
        The rates and the Poisson counts, each `[L, S, h]`.
    """
    return jax.vmap(lambda k, x, s: random_walk(k, x, s, h))(keys, x0, sigma)

    bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters.renewal ¶

    The PyRenew renewal model behind the repository's interfaces.

    The model itself (JAX, NumPyro, PyRenew) is in bdbvhubrenewal.model. It is imported lazily, so this module and the registry work without the model extra. This module owns everything around it:

    • the variants (VARIANTS), registered as models for the backtest;
    • vintage_inputs: a ForecastTask as the model's Vintage, with the leave-one-province-out mask;
    • samples_table: trajectories as the hub sample table, with the unassigned national component;
    • ppc_rows, parameter_diagnostics, chain_diagnostics: the CI's ppc.json and diagnostics.json;
    • delay_summary and fit_delays: each fit's learnt delay, written as delay-summary.csv beside its forecasts;
    • fit_renewal and forecast_renewal: the fit and forecast of the main and bvd fit configurations (bdbvhubrenewal.submission.fitting).

    This module reads only ModelConfig, MAIN, BVD, build_model, model_args, model.EXTRA_FIELDS, forecast_trajectories and adapter.vintage_from_tables from the subpackage, so a new model version drops in if it keeps those. Sampling is here (run_nuts), so the CI's sampler table applies in full.

    HUB_MODEL module-attribute ¶

    HUB_MODEL: Final = 'renewal'

    The model every fit configuration reports in its records.

    It is the internal key. The hub id is set apart, in config/hub.toml.

    SAMPLER_ENV module-attribute ¶

    SAMPLER_ENV: Final = 'BDBV_RENEWAL_SAMPLER'

    Environment variable with JSON sampler settings for registered models.

    DEFAULT_SAMPLER: Final[Mapping[str, Any]] = {

}

    Most provinces fitted at once by default, so a large shared host is not filled by one fit.

    @dataclass
class RenewalModel:
    """A renewal variant as a `ForecastModel`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    variant : Variant
        The variant.
    sampler : dict
        NUTS settings (`sampler_settings`).
    progress : pathlib.Path or None
        File to append progress lines to.
    supports_mask : bool
        The model honours `ForecastTask.mask`.
    name : str
        The variant name.
    delay_summary : pandas.DataFrame or None
        `fit_delays` of the last `forecast`.
    """

    variant: Variant
    sampler: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=sampler_settings)
    progress: Path | None = None
    supports_mask: bool = field(init=False, default=True)
    name: str = field(init=False)
    fit_diagnostics: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(
        init=False, default_factory=list
    )
    delay_summary: pd.DataFrame | None = field(init=False, default=None)

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Name the model after its variant and say if it takes a mask."""
        self.name = self.variant.name
        # A province fitted on its own cannot be forecast without its data.
        self.supports_mask = not self.variant.per_province

    def _log(self, line: str) -> None:
        if self.progress is not None:
            with self.progress.open("a") as fh:
                fh.write(line + "\n")

    def run(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalRun:
        """Fit the variant to a task and draw trajectories.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        RenewalRun
            The fit and its draws.
        """
        pr = engine()
        config = model_config(self.variant)
        rows, used = None, None
        if config.bvd:
            from bdbvhubrenewal.data import bvd

            release = bvd_release(task)
            used = bvd_record(release)
            if release is not None:
                rows = bvd.model_rows(release)
            rhat = used.get("joint_max_rhat")
            self._log(
                f"variant={self.name} bvd={used['tag'] or 'none'} "
                f"bvd_as_of={used.get('as_of', 'none')} "
                f"bvd_joint_rhat={'none' if rhat is None else f'{rhat:.3f}'}"
            )
        data = vintage_inputs(task, config, bvd=rows)
        model = pr.build_model(data, config)
        s = self.sampler
        self._log(f"variant={self.name} sampling start")
        start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
        run_nuts(model, data, {"seed": task.seed, **s})
        # Pulling the draws to the host waits for the sampler.
        np.asarray(next(iter(model.mcmc.get_samples().values())))
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
        cpu_seconds = time.process_time() - cpu_start
        self._log(
            f"variant={self.name} sampling done seconds={seconds:.0f} "
            f"cpu_seconds={cpu_seconds:.0f}"
        )
        draws = pr.forecast_trajectories(
            model,
            data,
            task.n_samples,
            seed=task.seed,
            as_of=tuple(report_cutoffs(task, data)),
        )
        by_chain = model.mcmc.get_samples(group_by_chain=True)
        trace = {
            k: np.asarray(by_chain[k])
            for k in model.mcmc.last_state.z
            if k in by_chain
        }
        extra = {
            k: np.asarray(v)
            for k, v in model.mcmc.get_extra_fields(group_by_chain=True).items()
        }
        posterior = model.mcmc.get_samples()
        n_init = model.latent.n_initialization_points
        beta = np.asarray(posterior["delay_beta"])
        # Each province's delay, and the shared one they pool towards
        # when a fit has more than one.
        shifts = {
            name: np.asarray(posterior["delay_shift"])[..., p]
            for p, name in enumerate(data.names)
        }
        if len(shifts) > 1:
            shifts["shared"] = np.asarray(posterior["delay_shared_shift"])[
                ..., 0
            ]
        delay = pd.concat(
            [
                delay_summary(
                    beta,
                    shift,
                    data.start_date - dt.timedelta(days=n_init),
                    n_init + data.cutoff,
                ).assign(place=place)
                for place, shift in shifts.items()
            ],
            ignore_index=True,
        )
        return RenewalRun(
            self.variant,
            data,
            draws,
            trace,
            extra,
            seconds,
            cpu_seconds,
            delay,
            used,
        )

    def forecast_fit(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalFit:
        """Fit the variant to a task and return its samples.

        A per-province variant fits each province on its own, apart from
        the provinces the random walks find silent (no case in their
        walk window), which take `randomwalknowcast`'s draws: exactly 0
        until an introduction, then its walk. Otherwise the provinces are
        fitted together. National is the sum of the provinces plus the
        unassigned part, the national cases no province has
        (`data_gap`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        RenewalFit
            The runs, province samples and national or unassigned parts.
        """
        frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        later: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        tasks = {"all": task}
        if self.variant.per_province:
            walk, silent = _silent_walk(task)
            frames.append(walk)
            later.extend(
                walk.loc[walk["target_end_date"] <= d].assign(as_of=d)
                for d in task.report_by
            )
            tasks = {
                loc: replace(task, locations=(loc,), mask=())
                for loc in task.locations
                if loc not in silent
            }
        runs = self._run_all(tasks)
        for key, run in runs.items():
            frames.append(samples_table(tasks[key], run.data, run.draws))
            later.extend(_as_reported(tasks[key], run))
        samples = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
        return RenewalFit(
            runs,
            samples,
            data_gap(task, samples),
            as_reported=pd.concat(later, ignore_index=True) if later else None,
        )

    def _run_all(self, tasks: Mapping[str, ForecastTask]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Run every task, largest first, `province_workers` at a time.

        Returns
        -------
        dict
            `RenewalRun` by key, in the order of `tasks`.
        """

        def size(key: str) -> float:
            target = tasks[key].target
            own = target["location"].isin(tasks[key].locations)
            return float(target.loc[own, "total"].sum())

        order = sorted(tasks, key=size, reverse=True)
        chains = int(self.sampler.get("num_chains", 1))
        workers = province_workers(chains, len(tasks))
        if workers == 1:
            done = {key: self.run(tasks[key]) for key in order}
        else:
            context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
            with ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, mp_context=context) as pool:
                futures = {
                    key: pool.submit(self.run, tasks[key]) for key in order
                }
                try:
                    done = {key: f.result() for key, f in futures.items()}
                except BaseException:
                    # Fail now, not after the queued fits have run.
                    pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)
                    raise
        return {key: done[key] for key in tasks}

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Return joint sample trajectories for a task.

        Parameters
        ----------
        task : ForecastTask
            The task.

        Returns
        -------
        pandas.DataFrame
            Columns `SAMPLE_COLUMNS`. With `task.report_by`, also `as_of`
            rows (`RenewalFit.as_reported`).

        Examples
        --------
        Fitting takes minutes per task on a CPU.

        >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import get_model
        >>> model = get_model("renewal")
        >>> samples = model.forecast(task)
        >>> model.fit_diagnostics  # divergences and R-hat of the fit
        """
        fit = self.forecast_fit(task)
        self.delay_summary = fit_delays(fit, task)
        self.fit_diagnostics = [
            {"fit": key, **fit_summary(run, self.sampler)}
            for key, run in fit.runs.items()
        ]
        samples = fit.samples
        if not task.report_by:
            return samples
        later = [] if fit.as_reported is None else [fit.as_reported]
        return pd.concat(
            [samples.assign(as_of=np.nan), *later], ignore_index=True
        )

    def run(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalRun:
    """Fit the variant to a task and draw trajectories.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.

    Returns
    -------
    RenewalRun
        The fit and its draws.
    """
    pr = engine()
    config = model_config(self.variant)
    rows, used = None, None
    if config.bvd:
        from bdbvhubrenewal.data import bvd

        release = bvd_release(task)
        used = bvd_record(release)
        if release is not None:
            rows = bvd.model_rows(release)
        rhat = used.get("joint_max_rhat")
        self._log(
            f"variant={self.name} bvd={used['tag'] or 'none'} "
            f"bvd_as_of={used.get('as_of', 'none')} "
            f"bvd_joint_rhat={'none' if rhat is None else f'{rhat:.3f}'}"
        )
    data = vintage_inputs(task, config, bvd=rows)
    model = pr.build_model(data, config)
    s = self.sampler
    self._log(f"variant={self.name} sampling start")
    start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.process_time()
    run_nuts(model, data, {"seed": task.seed, **s})
    # Pulling the draws to the host waits for the sampler.
    np.asarray(next(iter(model.mcmc.get_samples().values())))
    seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
    cpu_seconds = time.process_time() - cpu_start
    self._log(
        f"variant={self.name} sampling done seconds={seconds:.0f} "
        f"cpu_seconds={cpu_seconds:.0f}"
    )
    draws = pr.forecast_trajectories(
        model,
        data,
        task.n_samples,
        seed=task.seed,
        as_of=tuple(report_cutoffs(task, data)),
    )
    by_chain = model.mcmc.get_samples(group_by_chain=True)
    trace = {
        k: np.asarray(by_chain[k])
        for k in model.mcmc.last_state.z
        if k in by_chain
    }
    extra = {
        k: np.asarray(v)
        for k, v in model.mcmc.get_extra_fields(group_by_chain=True).items()
    }
    posterior = model.mcmc.get_samples()
    n_init = model.latent.n_initialization_points
    beta = np.asarray(posterior["delay_beta"])
    # Each province's delay, and the shared one they pool towards
    # when a fit has more than one.
    shifts = {
        name: np.asarray(posterior["delay_shift"])[..., p]
        for p, name in enumerate(data.names)
    }
    if len(shifts) > 1:
        shifts["shared"] = np.asarray(posterior["delay_shared_shift"])[
            ..., 0
        ]
    delay = pd.concat(
        [
            delay_summary(
                beta,
                shift,
                data.start_date - dt.timedelta(days=n_init),
                n_init + data.cutoff,
            ).assign(place=place)
            for place, shift in shifts.items()
        ],
        ignore_index=True,
    )
    return RenewalRun(
        self.variant,
        data,
        draws,
        trace,
        extra,
        seconds,
        cpu_seconds,
        delay,
        used,
    )

    def forecast_fit(self, task: ForecastTask) -> RenewalFit:
    """Fit the variant to a task and return its samples.

    A per-province variant fits each province on its own, apart from
    the provinces the random walks find silent (no case in their
    walk window), which take `randomwalknowcast`'s draws: exactly 0
    until an introduction, then its walk. Otherwise the provinces are
    fitted together. National is the sum of the provinces plus the
    unassigned part, the national cases no province has
    (`data_gap`).

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.

    Returns
    -------
    RenewalFit
        The runs, province samples and national or unassigned parts.
    """
    frames: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    later: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
    tasks = {"all": task}
    if self.variant.per_province:
        walk, silent = _silent_walk(task)
        frames.append(walk)
        later.extend(
            walk.loc[walk["target_end_date"] <= d].assign(as_of=d)
            for d in task.report_by
        )
        tasks = {
            loc: replace(task, locations=(loc,), mask=())
            for loc in task.locations
            if loc not in silent
        }
    runs = self._run_all(tasks)
    for key, run in runs.items():
        frames.append(samples_table(tasks[key], run.data, run.draws))
        later.extend(_as_reported(tasks[key], run))
    samples = pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True)
    return RenewalFit(
        runs,
        samples,
        data_gap(task, samples),
        as_reported=pd.concat(later, ignore_index=True) if later else None,
    )

    def forecast(self, task: ForecastTask) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Return joint sample trajectories for a task.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.

    Returns
    -------
    pandas.DataFrame
        Columns `SAMPLE_COLUMNS`. With `task.report_by`, also `as_of`
        rows (`RenewalFit.as_reported`).

    Examples
    --------
    Fitting takes minutes per task on a CPU.

    >>> from bdbvhubrenewal.forecasters import get_model
    >>> model = get_model("renewal")
    >>> samples = model.forecast(task)
    >>> model.fit_diagnostics  # divergences and R-hat of the fit
    """
    fit = self.forecast_fit(task)
    self.delay_summary = fit_delays(fit, task)
    self.fit_diagnostics = [
        {"fit": key, **fit_summary(run, self.sampler)}
        for key, run in fit.runs.items()
    ]
    samples = fit.samples
    if not task.report_by:
        return samples
    later = [] if fit.as_reported is None else [fit.as_reported]
    return pd.concat(
        [samples.assign(as_of=np.nan), *later], ignore_index=True
    )

    def province_workers(num_chains: int, n_provinces: int) -> int:
    """Return how many provinces a per-province variant fits at once.

    `PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV` if set, else one fit per `num_chains` cores,
    at most `MAX_PROVINCE_WORKERS`: with parallel chains (the policy's
    setting) each chain then has a core. Never more than the provinces.

    Parameters
    ----------
    num_chains : int
        Chains of each fit, run in parallel.
    n_provinces : int
        Provinces to fit.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        At least 1.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV` is not a positive integer.
    """
    env = os.environ.get(PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV)
    if env:
        if not env.isdigit() or int(env) < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{PROVINCE_WORKERS_ENV} must be a positive integer, "
                f"got {env!r}."
            )
        workers = int(env)
    else:
        workers = min(MAX_PROVINCE_WORKERS, _cores() // max(1, num_chains))
    return max(1, min(workers, n_provinces))

    def nuts_kernel(model_fn: Any, sampler: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """Build the NUTS kernel for a sampler table.

    Each chain starts from its own prior draw, so chains start apart and
    R-hat can show a chain that stays in another mode.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model_fn : callable
        The NumPyro model.
    sampler : mapping
        `target_accept` and `max_tree_depth`.

    Returns
    -------
    numpyro.infer.NUTS
        The kernel.
    """
    from numpyro.infer import NUTS, init_to_sample

    return NUTS(
        model_fn,
        target_accept_prob=float(sampler["target_accept"]),
        max_tree_depth=int(sampler["max_tree_depth"]),
        init_strategy=init_to_sample,
    )

    def run_nuts(model: Any, data: Any, sampler: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:
    """Fit a built model by NUTS, keeping the fields the diagnostics need.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : pyrenew.model.MultiSignalModel
        From `build_model`.
    data : bdbvhubrenewal.model.Vintage
        The inputs.
    sampler : mapping
        The full sampler table (`sampler_settings`).

    Returns
    -------
    pyrenew.model.MultiSignalModel
        The model, with `model.mcmc` holding the posterior.
    """
    import jax
    from jax import random
    from numpyro.infer import MCMC

    # Each fit compiles its own model, so cached executables from earlier
    # fits never help and exhaust LLVM memory over many locations.
    jax.clear_caches()  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
    pr = engine()
    args = pr.model_args(model, data)
    model.validate_data(
        **{k: v for k, v in args.items() if k != "population_size"}
    )
    model.mcmc = MCMC(
        nuts_kernel(model.sample, sampler),
        num_warmup=int(sampler["num_warmup"]),
        num_samples=int(sampler["num_samples"]),
        num_chains=int(sampler["num_chains"]),
        chain_method=str(sampler.get("chain_method", "vectorized")),
        progress_bar=False,
    )
    model.mcmc.run(
        random.key(int(sampler["seed"])),
        extra_fields=pr.model.EXTRA_FIELDS,
        **args,
    )
    return model

    def horizon_weeks(task: ForecastTask) -> int:
    """Weeks the model must run past the week holding the vintage.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task : ForecastTask
        The task.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        At least one.
    """
    last = max(_saturday(d) for d in task.target_end_dates)
    return max(1, (last - _saturday(task.cutoff)).days // 7)

    """Return the BVDOutbreakSize release chosen for a task's vintage.

    The newest release that existed at the vintage's cut-off and whose
